problem.statement: Count connected groups of 1s in a 2D grid using 4-direction adjacency.

grid.meaning: The 2D collection containing cells to inspect.

r.meaning: The row coordinate of the current grid cell.

c.meaning: The column coordinate of the current grid cell.

count.meaning: The number of distinct connected groups discovered so far.

stack.meaning: The grid positions pending iterative traversal.

representation_requirements.description: Represent each inspected cell using its row and column coordinates.
Represent adjacency using the four orthogonal directions.
Represent whether an eligible cell has already been discovered or traversed.
Represent pending cells for iterative connected-component traversal.
Represent the accumulated number of distinct connected groups.

semantic_invariants.statement: Cells belong to the same group only when connected through orthogonal neighbors.
A group is counted exactly when an eligible undiscovered cell is identified as a new starting point.
Traversal visits every eligible cell reachable from the starting point through orthogonal adjacency.
Traversal does not process positions outside the grid boundaries.
The count equals the number of distinct eligible connected groups discovered so far.
After all cells are processed, the count equals the total number of distinct connected groups.

completion_evidence.description: The learner identifies the grid-cell representation and the four orthogonal adjacency relationships.
The learner distinguishes a new eligible undiscovered starting cell from a cell already belonging to a traversed group.
The learner tracks row, column, and stack state while extending traversal through eligible orthogonal neighbors.
The learner connects one count increment to each discovered group and identifies completion after the grid is processed.

terminal_behavior: When all grid cells are processed, return the accumulated count of distinct connected groups.
When no eligible cells exist, return a count of zero.
When traversal reaches a boundary or ineligible cell, do not extend traversal through that position.
When an eligible cell has already been discovered, do not count it as a new group.
